blocks.text: Dear Ms. Frazier:

This letter sets down the terms on which our firm will act for {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} on the cost transformation we have discussed, and, once you have countersigned it, it will stand as the agreement between us. I have written it in the plain manner we prefer for such things, so that it reads as a faithful account of the conversation we had rather than as an instrument to be read against either of us, and I would ask you, before you sign, to measure it against your own memory of what was said and to tell me of anything that sits at odds with it.
The Work We Have Agreed to Undertake

The engagement is directed at the cost structure of {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} and at the practical question of where cost has settled that no longer earns the company anything, which is a different question from where cost is merely large, and we will keep the two apart with some care. We will work from your own ledgers rather than from a template, on the understanding that the budget records what the business meant to spend while the ledger records what it actually spent, and it is the second of those that a cost transformation has to begin from if its conclusions are to hold.

Our approach will be unhurried in its early weeks and deliberately so. We will first reconcile the cost base until neither side has cause to argue later about the denominator, then benchmark it against a comparator set we will agree with you, and only then form a view of what can responsibly be taken out and in what order the organization can absorb it. What the engagement is meant to deliver is a set of choices your leadership can own, supported by evidence your own people can rerun after we have gone; it is not meant to deliver a recommendation that arrives faster than the analysis beneath it can bear.
The People You Will Work With

Michael Walker will manage the engagement day to day and will be the person you deal with most often; he runs the workstream from end to end and is accustomed to carrying a client's question and the firm's answer across the same table without losing either. James Green will build and maintain the cost model and the exhibits that our findings will rest on, and Deborah Gordon will own the benchmarking and the data-heavy work that sits behind it; both of them keep to the firm's habit of letting a figure be traced back through the file to the place it came from. I will keep my own hand on the engagement at the points where a judgment must be made about how far a finding can be pressed before it outruns what we actually know, and nothing of consequence will leave the firm under our name without my having read it first.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2009-001.fee}}, which covers the time of the people named above through the expected close of the work. We will render invoices against that amount as the engagement proceeds, and each will be payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time and not the incidental costs of the work, such as travel or the reproduction of materials, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us; should the shape of the work change materially from what this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will settle it together before any further work begins, so that nothing ever reaches you on an invoice as a surprise.
Term and Termination

The engagement will begin on {{fact:f:E-2009-001.start}} and is expected to run for something on the order of seven months, though we will treat it as complete when the work is genuinely done and not merely when the calendar has turned. Either of us may bring it to an end on fourteen days' written notice to the other; if you choose to do so, you will owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} in the course of this work we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement. That obligation binds every member of our team, it survives the close of the work, and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We would ask the same of you in respect of the methods and the written materials we share with you, which represent the firm's own way of working.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the decisions your leadership will ultimately take on the strength of our work, nor the conditions of the markets in which you operate, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder of it will continue in force, unaffected.

If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, I would be grateful if you would sign one copy where indicated below and return it to us, keeping the other for your file; once your signed copy is in our hands, Michael Walker will write to you to fix the first meetings and the opening requests for information, so that we can begin without delay.

To: James Green, Deborah Gordon
From: Michael Walker
Re: Getting the cost transformation for {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} under way

The purpose of this memo is to fix who owns what before we begin, so that we start in step rather than sort it out on the fly. The engagement commences on {{fact:f:E-2009-001.start}} and runs for roughly seven months; our sponsor on the client side is Sandra Frazier, VP Finance, and I will be the single point of contact with her so that {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} hears one voice from us.

The aim of the first phase is narrow and worth stating plainly: to build a cost baseline that both sides will accept before anyone argues about what to do with it. Everything that follows, the benchmarking and the read on where cost can responsibly come out, stands on that baseline, so the early weeks are about getting the numbers clean and agreed rather than about reaching a conclusion.

A second point is worth setting down at the outset, which is that we work from the client's ledger and not from its budget, on the understanding that the budget records what the business meant to spend while the ledger records what it actually spent. Where the two diverge is often the most useful thing we find, so keep the divergence rather than smoothing it, and note it plainly in the file where you find it.
The work in front of us

items: Cost baseline. James Green will assemble the combined cost base from the client's general ledger, reconcile it against the departmental allocations so that it ties out, and stand up the model that the rest of the analysis will run on; where a number will not reconcile, flag it rather than force it.

Benchmarking. Deborah Gordon will build the comparator set and the benchmarks against it, keeping every source on file so that any figure we later put in front of the client can be traced back to where it came from, and labeling as provisional anything the comparators do not yet support.

Data and access. I will run the requests for information to Sandra Frazier's team and keep a running index of what has arrived and what is still outstanding, so that neither of you has to chase the client directly and so that our status to her rests on one accurate list.

Working record. From the first week we will keep one shared engagement file, so that our status notes and exhibits draw from a single record and not from anyone's memory of it, and so that the client's own people could rerun the analysis after we have gone.

blocks.text: How we start the week

For the coming week the priority is simply access and materials. I will send {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} the opening request for information on the first day, and I would ask each of you to send me, by the end of the week, the list of documents and contacts your area needs, so that I can fold it into one request to the client rather than several.

James Green, please treat the general-ledger extract and the departmental cost allocations as the two items to press for first, since the model cannot begin without them. Deborah Gordon, you can start the comparator scan in parallel so that we are not idle while the client's data comes in, and I will bring you in on the reconciliation the moment the ledger lands so that the benchmarks are built on numbers we have already checked.

I will circulate the standing check-in schedule once Sandra Frazier and I have agreed a cadence, and I will keep the shared file current so that no one has to ask me twice for the same status. If anything on the client side threatens the timeline, raise it with me early and I will handle it with Sandra Frazier's team; a data pull that slips by a week costs us little if we know about it, and a good deal if we learn of it late.
Dear Sandra,

The cost baseline for the {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} engagement is coming together, and the one thing that will keep it on schedule is the next tranche of ledger detail from your team. James Green has the general-ledger extract loaded and is reconciling it now, and Deborah Gordon has begun the benchmarking against the comparator set we agreed at kickoff.

What we still need to close out the baseline is the departmental cost allocations and the vendor spend file for the trailing year. If you can point us to whoever maintains those two, I will take the detail from them directly and keep it off your desk; our aim is to have the baseline reconciled and agreed with your finance team before we draw a single conclusion from it.

It would also help to hold a short working call this week to walk the reconciliation. On our side that would be James Green, Deborah Gordon, and Michael Walker; from yours, I would suggest Sandra Frazier and the owner of the allocations, so that any question on the numbers can be answered in the room. Let me know a half hour that suits you and I will send an agenda the day before.
Regards
Dear Sandra,

Thank you for turning the allocations around so quickly. They reached us on Friday, James Green has already folded them into the baseline, and the reconciliation now ties out to within a rounding difference on the {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} numbers, which is exactly where we want it before we benchmark.

The one remaining gap is the vendor spend file, which Deborah Gordon needs to finish the comparator work; if your team can send it across this week, we will hold the schedule without difficulty. I have flagged it as the single open item on the shared list so that nothing else is waiting behind it.

For the call itself, the aim is narrow: to walk the reconciliation line by line so that your team and ours are agreed on the baseline before we take the benchmarking any further. Nothing on our side is a conclusion yet, so please have your people come ready to press on the numbers; a question raised in the room is worth far more to us than a silent doubt.

On the working call we set for later this week, I have us down as James Green, Deborah Gordon, and Michael Walker from our side, with Sandra Frazier and the allocations owner from yours. I will send a short agenda the day before so that we keep it to the half hour.
Regards
Cost Transformation: {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}}
A progress briefing prepared for Sandra Frazier and the finance leadership by the Calderwood engagement team.
Where the engagement stands

We are in the current-state phase, building and reconciling the cost baseline for {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}}.
The baseline is substantially assembled; a small number of allocations are still being agreed with your finance team.
Nothing here is a recommendation yet; today is about the facts the later choices will rest on.

items: Michael Walker, Engagement Manager, is your day-to-day point of contact.
James Green builds and maintains the cost model and the exhibits behind it.
Deborah Gordon owns the benchmarking and the comparator analysis.

blocks.text: What the baseline shows so far

items: Cost concentrates in a small number of functions, more so than the budget alone would suggest.
The support functions carry the clearest overlap and are the first place we will test for savings that are real rather than nominal.
A share of the apparent duplication is tied to standing commitments, and we will keep what can be realized soon separate from what depends on those running their course.

Where the near-term savings are dependable as against where they only appear on paper.
How to protect the parts of the business that are already performing while the work proceeds.

blocks.text: Minutes: Working Session on the Cost Transformation for {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}}

These are the minutes of the working session we held with the client team to walk the emerging cost baseline and to agree what we would test next. We are roughly at the midpoint of the engagement, and the session was meant less to settle anything than to make sure the two sides are working from the same numbers before we turn to what can come out of them.
Present

items: Michael Walker, Engagement Manager, Calderwood Partners
James Green, Senior Associate, Calderwood Partners
Deborah Gordon, Associate, Calderwood Partners
Sandra Frazier, VP Finance, {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}}

blocks.text: What we discussed

Michael Walker opened by reminding us where the work stands, and Mike was careful to keep the analysis and any recommendation clearly apart, on the view that {{fact:f:E-2009-001.client}} should agree the facts before anyone is asked to agree what to do about them. James Green then walked the group through the reconciled baseline, which now ties out against the departmental allocations, and noted the handful of allocations still being settled between the two finance teams. He was clear that the baseline should be treated as firm everywhere except in those few lines, which he has marked in the file so that no one builds on them before they are closed.

I took the group through the benchmarking as it stands, and we spent most of the session on where the comparators suggest cost has settled without buying the business anything. We were careful not to overstate what the comparators show, since the sample is still being filled out, and I flagged the two functions where our read is firmest and the one where it is not yet firm at all. Sandra Frazier was helpful in cautioning us that a share of the apparent duplication reflects commitments that cannot be unwound quickly, and we agreed that our read on savings should keep what can be realized in the near term separate from what depends on those commitments running their course.

We closed the discussion by naming the questions the second half of the work turns on, which are the order in which cost can responsibly come out, the savings that can be relied upon as against those that are merely nominal, and the safeguards that keep the parts of the business that are working from being disturbed while we proceed. Nothing was presented as settled, and we agreed to hold that line until both finance teams have signed off on the figures beneath it.
What we agreed to do

rows: Close the remaining cost allocations with the two finance teams and lock the reconciled baseline
Finish the benchmarking and draft the first read on addressable cost, with near-term savings kept separate from committed spend
Confirm the finance owner for the allocation sign-off and flag any commitments that cannot be unwound quickly
Set the next working session and agree the agenda with the client

blocks.text: The next working session will be set once the savings read is drafted, and our single next step is to get the outstanding allocations closed this week so that the baseline can be locked. These minutes will stand as the record of what we agreed unless a correction reaches me within the week.
